newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik 1996 raw cotton harvest seen low 340,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Tajik 1996 raw cotton harvest seen low 340,000 T.

text.p: The former Soviet republic of Tajikistan's 1996 cotton harvest was unlikely to exceed 340,000 tonnes, far below last year's 417,000 tonnes, a senior Tajik agricultural official said on Friday.

"We have so far harvested 210,000 tonnes (of raw cotton)," Shukrullo Rasim Nazarov, head of the industrial crops department at Tajikistan's agriculture ministry, told Reuters. "We don't expect to harvest more than 340,000 tonnes this year."
In Soviet times, the remote, mountainous republic produced up to 900,000 tonnes of cotton annually.
Nazarov said Tajikistan planned to export 70 percent of its cotton harvest this year.
All economic activity in Tajikistan has been hit hard by a bloody four-year civil war.
Nazarov blamed the lower harvest outlook on a lack of fertilisers, which he said had reduced yields to 1.7 tonnes per hectare in 1995, down from the Soviet-era average of four tonnes per hectare.
